failure_summary.description: Tool name was the Provider tagline ('Rocket League — Ranks, stats…', 'Flightera Flight Data — …'), or only the provider or only the API ('BestBuy Product Data', 'Zappos product detail by Product ID') instead of the exact '### Provider: API' heading.
A repeated 'optional parameters' key was appended after a filled list, or two calls were merged into one object with duplicate 'tool name' keys. This wiped out parameters and lost whole calls.

Long narrative or vague queries were only partly covered: 3 of 10 calls in one, 1 of 3-4 in another, and Lost Ark and Rocket League endpoints collapsed together in a third. Missing calls include the Wayfair search, Asos countries, autocomplete, Aliexpress, Amazon, currencies, airport data and per-city lookups.

Inputs were attached to the wrong clause (role-account domain reused from another clause). Plain disposable and 'suggest' disposable siblings were swapped. A generic game-search tool was used instead of the named Zelda tool. A Ranks tool was called with an invented 'player' value. The dice-rolls tool was used for 'three dice'.
Query-implied qualifiers were dropped or wrong: count 25 for chess puzzles, lang 'en' instead of 'en-US', and the demo key and minLength lost to key duplication.

patch.reasoning: Tool-name format is still the largest failure source: the model copies the Provider tagline or only half of the name. A mechanical rule with wrong/right examples should fix that. Duplicate-key and merged-object JSON errors are the second source, so an explicit per-object self-check is added. Long or vague queries are under-covered, so there is guidance to enumerate every clause and to pick topic tools that need only the stated inputs, with no placeholders. Clause-to-input binding, sibling disambiguation and provider-named tool choice caused several wrong calls, so they get compact rules. The edits are few and concrete, since the large multi-rule patch in step 6 was rejected.

edits.target: Never give only the provider or only the endpoint, even when the query names the tool loosely.
edits.content: Never give only the provider or only the endpoint, even when the query names the tool loosely (query says 'the BestBuy Product Data tool' -> `BestBuy Product Data: BestBuyProductData`; 'Zappos product detail by Product ID' -> `Zappos Realtime Data: Zappos product detail by Product ID`). Build the name mechanically: it is the text after `### ` in that tool's block. NEVER use the text of the `Provider:` line (the long tagline after the dash, e.g. `Rocket League — Ranks, stats, news & more…`) and never put ` — ` in a tool name. When one provider has several endpoints (Lost Ark, Rocket League, Wayfair, fast Email verifier, Dice Roll Simulator), each call needs its own full `Provider: API` name.

edits.target: Do not close the list early or leave stray brackets.
edits.content: - Self-check every object before answering: `{"tool name": ..., "required parameters": [...], "optional parameters": [...]}`, closed with `}`. The string `"optional parameters"` appears exactly once per object. Never append a second `"optional parameters": []` after a filled list, and never put a second `"tool name"` or a second parameter set inside one object. Every call, even to the same tool or in the same sentence, is its own `{...}`. Each parameter (e.g. a demo `X-RapidAPI-Key`, `minLength`) goes once into the list the schema assigns.

edits.target: - Do not add 'helper', 'random', 'new releases' or 'list' calls that no clause names.
edits.content:
- Long or narrative queries ('searched X, focused on SKU Y, exploring A, B and C ... They also investigated other platforms: ...') need one call per action across the WHOLE query, including every sentence after 'also', 'then' or a colon. The opening verb counts too ('searched for chairs on Wayfair' -> the Wayfair search call, even when a SKU follows). Map noun phrases to endpoints: 'categories and country availability' -> categories list + countries list; 'regional settings' -> the user/region-parameters endpoint; 'a specific store (ID, seller ID)' -> the store endpoint with both ids; 'ASIN on the German marketplace' -> product endpoint with domain `de`. Count your calls against the query's items before answering; stopping after the first sentence's items is a common miss.
- Vague or topic-only queries ('flights between Winnipeg and London, currency exchange rates, airport data for both locations') get one call per topic from the tool that needs only the stated inputs: currency -> the currencies endpoint; 'airport data' -> the airport-data endpoint; each named place -> one location lookup/autocomplete call with that place as the `string`/query value (set airport/city flags `true` when airports or cities are asked for). Never choose a tool whose required value the query does not give (flight number, hotel id, player name), and never invent a value or placeholder such as `player` or a made-up flight number.

- Bind each input to its own clause: copy the value from the clause that names that action ('disposable-mail.xyz for role accounts' -> Role Account with domain `disposable-mail.xyz`; do not reuse another clause's input). A bare domain goes in a `domain` parameter, never an `email` parameter.
- When two clauses ask for the same kind of check on different inputs, let the clause words pick the sibling: 'disposable domain with suggested alternatives' -> the tool named '...Suggest Domain'; a plain 'is X a disposable domain' -> the plain domain-disposable tool (e.g. `MailCheck: Domain`).
- A provider or game named in the clause wins over generic tools: 'for The Legend of Zelda, search games with Majora, limited to 25' -> the Zelda games-list tool (name `Majora`, limit `25`), not a generic game-search tool. 'Three regular dice' -> the dice-count tool (`dice`=`3`); use the 'rolls' tool only when the query also gives a number of rolls. '25 chess puzzles' -> count `25`. 'US market in English' -> country `US`, lang `en-US`.
